title: Claude Code governance
subtitle: Author managed policy, hooks, MCP and sandbox controls, and Cedar/OPA policy-as-code — and review the policy-vs-observed drift the engine reports.

hitl.vaultsRisk: Lateral risk: vaults/credentials are workspace-scoped — anyone with a workspace API key can reference them. Secrets are write-only; archive purges secrets but retains records for audit, delete is a hard delete.

ms.legacyPath: The legacy Windows C:\ProgramData\ClaudeCode path is no longer supported (removed in {{since}}).

hooks.enforcementOff: Hook decision/enforcement is opt-in and OFF by default, and is governed by the approval gate when enabled. Authoring here emits policy — it does not make the system block on its own.

mcp.serverNameCaveat: A serverName-only allowlist is NOT a security control — match by exact URL/command.

sandbox.egressSub: Hosts Claude Code must be able to reach.

pdp.opaAuthoringOnly: OPA / Rego is authoring + export only: the embedded PDP is Cedar, and centralized decisions use AuthZEN. Rego is validated and versioned here, then enforced by YOUR OPA sidecar — it is never evaluated in-process, so dry-run imposes no restriction for OPA.
pdp.exampleSub: Evaluate the policy against this request (mirrors the engine's authorization input).
pdp.liveHint: Validate, decision-explain, dry-run, version history, the compile/validate gate, publish and activation are all served by the engine at /v1/m/governance/pdp.
pdp.cedarSemantics: Three-valued enforcement: a permit GRANTS the request within its resolved scope tree — beyond the RBAC baseline, and an RBAC denial is bypassed; a forbid RESTRICTS and overrides any grant; no match ABSTAINS, so the RBAC decision stands.
pdp.cedarSemanticsBounds: A grant never reaches outside the scope tree it resolves to (workspace / agent-group / resource), and while this node is offline past its policy staleness bound a grant degrades to abstain instead of continuing to authorize — a restriction stays enforced.
pdp.decisionFooter: This is a dry-run of an unpublished candidate. A permit grants within its scope tree, a forbid restricts and overrides any grant, and no match abstains so the RBAC decision stands; scope-tree conditions resolve against the live hierarchy only once the revision is activated.
pdp.decisionFooterOpa: Nothing is evaluated in this process for OPA: this dry-run imposes no restriction at all, and your own OPA sidecar owns Rego enforcement.

publish.confirmTitle: Publish and activate this Cedar policy?
publish.confirmBody: A new immutable revision is stored and selected, then the live Cedar engine is recompiled from the union of the authored, managed and adopted surfaces. From that moment a permit grants within its scope tree and a forbid restricts.
publish.confirmNote: Deny-closed: a source that does not compile is rejected before anything is stored, and the previously active policy keeps deciding. If the store commits but the live swap fails, the result says so explicitly.
publish.confirmBodyOpa: This stores an immutable revision of the Rego source and selects it in the authored history. Nothing is enforced from this action: your own OPA sidecar owns Rego enforcement, and this revision is not pushed to it from here.
publish.confirmNoteOpa: The local check is structural only — authoritative Rego compilation happens in your OPA sidecar.

rollback.confirmBody: This appends an activation record that selects {{engine}} revision r{{n}}. It does not create a new revision and it does not delete any later revision — the immutable history is preserved in full.
rollback.confirmNote: The target and the full Cedar union are compiled BEFORE the activation record is written; if that compile fails, the current selection is left unchanged.
rollback.confirmNoteOpa: Nothing is enforced from this action: your own OPA sidecar owns Rego enforcement, and this revision is not pushed to it from here.
rollback.previewUnavailable: Could not read the source of r{{n}}. Activate it only if you already know what it contains — an unreadable revision is not the same as an unchanged one.
rollback.previewNoActive: No revision is active yet, so there is nothing to compare against. This is the full source r{{n}} would put in force:
rollback.previewBaseUnavailable: Could not read which revision is currently active, so there is nothing to compare r{{n}} against. That is not the same as "nothing is active" — activate only if you already know the current state.

diff.title: Change to the authored surface
diff.subtitle: Your draft compared with the revision the store currently selects.
diff.noActive: No revision is active for this engine yet — publishing will create the first one, so there is nothing to compare against.
diff.unavailable: Cannot show the diff — the active revision could not be loaded. Publishing is disabled until it is, so a change is never made against an unknown baseline.
diff.publishBlocked: Publishing is disabled until the active revision loads.
diff.unionNote: The enforced Cedar policy is the UNION of three surfaces. This diff shows only the authored surface — the one this editor edits, and the only one a publish replaces.
diff.contentWithheld: The managed and adopted sources are not disclosed here: showing them would widen this read permission. Presence, revision and digest are enough to say that more is in force than what you edit.
diff.opaScope: Nothing is enforced from this console for OPA. This diff compares your draft with the revision selected in the authored Rego history; there is no managed or adopted Rego surface, and your own OPA sidecar owns Rego enforcement.
diff.surfacesUnknown: Could not read the active policy, so the contributing surfaces are unknown. That is NOT the same as there being none: what you edit may not be all that is in force.

result.appliedToast: Compiled and activated on this process's live engine.
result.deferredToast: Stored and selected, but NOT enforcing.
result.appliedTitle: Compiled and activated on this process
result.deferredTitle: Stored and selected — but NOT enforcing
result.appliedBody: Revision r{{n}} compiled and swapped on the live grant engine of THIS PROCESS. The selection is durable: the stored active revision is re-activated when the process restarts. Nothing propagates the swap between processes, so other replicas keep enforcing their loaded policy until they restart or recompose.
result.deferredBody: Revision r{{n}} is committed in the store and selected as active, but the live grant engine was NOT swapped: the PREVIOUS policy is still deciding requests on this process.
result.deferredRecovery: It re-activates on a process restart, on the next successful publish or activation, or on any scoped-grant or role write that recomposes the engine. There is no endpoint that reloads the PDP on demand, so there is no button here to press.
result.versionedBody: Revision r{{n}} is stored in the authored history and selected there. Nothing is enforced from this action — your own OPA sidecar owns Rego enforcement.
result.unknownToast: The engine did not report whether the policy is enforcing.
result.unknownBody: Revision r{{n}} was stored, but the engine did not report an activation state this console recognises. Do not read that as enforcing, and do not read it as harmless.

gate.title: Compile/validate gate
gate.subtitle: The stored result of the compile and validation gate that ran before this revision was committed. It is not a behavioral policy test suite — there has never been one.
gate.noActiveRevision: No {{engine}} revision is selected, so there is no stored gate result to show.
gate.unavailableNoReason: The engine reported no stored gate artifact and gave no reason.
gate.noResults: The engine reported the artifact as available but returned no result rows.
gate.activeRevisionUnknown: Could not read which revision is active, so there is no gate result to show. This does not mean no revision is active.

live.title: In force on this process
live.loading: Reading what this process is enforcing…
live.unknown: Could not find out whether this process is enforcing the selected revision. That does NOT mean it is not enforcing it — it means the answer could not be read.
live.appliedBody: This process is deciding requests with the revision the store selects.
live.deferredBody: This process is NOT deciding requests with the selected revision: a previously compiled policy is still in force here.
live.notApplicableBody: Nothing is enforced from this process for {{engine}} — your own OPA sidecar owns Rego enforcement.
live.processScope: Measured on the process that served this read. Nothing propagates an activation between processes, so another replica answers for itself.
live.noPolicyBody: The store selects no Cedar revision, so there is nothing in force from here. This is not a failure — it is a tenant that has not published a policy yet.
live.grantsExpired: This process is past its offline-staleness bound, so the policy's POSITIVE grants have degraded to abstain. Its forbid rules stay enforced. The policy IS loaded here — what expired is the trust in its grants.

dist.noArtifact: no signed artifact — nothing to pull
